claims.text: Local lattice distortions induced by atomic-size mismatch primarily govern the strength and deformation or failure behavior of multi-component concentrated alloys.
Atomic-size-induced lattice distortions impede dislocation motion.
Atomic-size-induced lattice distortions promote localized shear.
Local lattice distortion is more important than precipitation or grain-boundary mechanisms in the specified alloys.
Arc melting followed by homogenization heat treatment ensures a uniform microstructure in the proposed alloys.
A broader range of constituent atomic radii produces greater atomic-size mismatch and greater local lattice distortion.
The extent of local lattice distortion alters local stress fields.
Local stress fields created by lattice distortion act as obstacles to dislocation motion.
Accumulation of dislocations at distortion sites promotes shear localization.
Increased lattice distortion raises yield strength.
Minimizing lattice distortion permits more uniform dislocation motion.
The high-mismatch alloy will have higher dislocation densities localized around distortion fields than the baseline alloy.
The high-distortion alloy will exhibit broader X-ray diffraction peaks because of greater microstrain.
The proposed mechanism applies to homogeneous, single-phase concentrated alloys when precipitation and grain-boundary strengthening are absent or minimized.
The proposed mechanism is limited to deformation dominated by dislocations, such as room-temperature quasi-static loading.
Short-range chemical ordering, grain-boundary characteristics, and other microstructural features may also affect dislocation behavior and mechanical response.

contradictions.description: The intervention calls for alloy families with identical base elemental compositions while proposing that atomic-size mismatch be changed by selecting different elements; changing elemental identities conflicts with keeping elemental composition identical. The baseline further describes only a similar, rather than identical, elemental composition.
